metadata.Notes: The character descriptions are correct in programmes for performances in 1937-1939 and from 2004, but in revivals from 1940/41 to 1989, they contain mistakes. The word 'one' dropped out of the Four Guests's description; it should read 'They incline to oblige only one when they stare'. The descriptions of the Two Gendarmes and the Bridesmaids were transposed. The Gendarmes's description is 'They may recognise places' and the Bridesmaids' is 'They make preparations to deal with an exception'. Because of the length of time these mistakes appeared, the performance records in this database reflect the programmes, even if they are incorrect.

metadata.Description: Belt of dusky pink and mauve shot silk dupion embroidered in silk thread with a pattern of flowers and foliage in taupe, cream and dark blue. The outside of the belt is decorated along its length with four rows of faux pearls. It fastens with a hook and eye, on top of which is a decorative faux gold filigree lozenge. Hanging from it are seven strings of faux pearls of differing length. Six of them finish with a large pearl teardrop bead and one with a gold teardrop bead. Worn with robe ROH/PRO/COS/0005951, dress ROH/PRO/COS/0005954, underskirt ROH/PRO/COS/0005953, and shoes ROH/PRO/COS/0005956.

searchDocuments.title: Black and white photographic negatives of the Sadler's Wells Theatre Ballet at the Arts Theatre, Cambridge
searchDocuments.subtitle: Roger Wood Photographic Collection | 23 July 1951 - 28 July 1951

metadata.Date notes: Negatives are dated July 1951; exact dates derived from research.
metadata.Extent: 94 single 2.25" x 2.25" black and white negatives
metadata.Scope and content: Negatives featuring members of the company in costume for 'Assembly Ball' and 'Valses nobles et sentimentales'; company members with conductor John Lanchbery backstage in the wings and in their dressing rooms; the stage crew hanging the stage cloths; Stella Claire, Pirmin Trecu, assistant ballet mistress Barbara Fewster and stage manager Valerie West in a Cambridge tearoom; and David Blair, Svetlana Beriosova, and Elaine Fifield punting on the river Cam.
metadata.Creator: Roger Wood
metadata.Publication note: Five images from these negatives appear in R.Wood, A.Haskell, J.Hall, 'The Theatre Ballet of Sadler's Wells in photographs by Roger Wood'. London: Phoenix House Ltd, 1952, pp28, 29, 31, 32.

searchDocuments.title: Black and white photographic negatives of the Sadler's Wells Theatre Ballet company outside Sadler's Wells Theatre, London
searchDocuments.subtitle: Roger Wood Photographic Collection | 7 June 1951

metadata.Date notes: Negatives are dated.
metadata.Extent: 11 single 2.25" x 2.25" black and white negatives
metadata.Scope and content: Negatives of a group portrait of the company taken outside the Sadler's Wells Theatre. Peggy van Praagh is seated at the front with the following people behind left to right: Elaine Fifield, David Blair and Svetlana Beriosova; Donald Britton, Maryon Lane, David Poole, Patricia Miller, and Sheilah O'Reilly; Michael Hogan, Yvonne Barnes, Stella Claire, Annette Page, Peter Wright, Veronica Vail, David Gill and Pauline Harrop; Shirley Bishop, Joan Cadzow, Donald Gillies, Tony Tarver, Donald McAlpine, Maurice Metliss, and Sara Neil; Joanne Nisbet, Arnott Mader, Madeleine White, Graham McCormack, and Romayne Austin; John Lanchbery, Valerie West, Ursula Moreton, Barbara Fewster, and Ian Keith. Negatives also feature Svetlana Beriosova, Elaine Fifield, and David Blair walking past the front of the theatre.
metadata.Creator: Roger Wood

metadata.Description: Polyester satin sleeveless padded bodysuit with attached knee-length legs. The front of the bodysuit is terracotta coloured satin and the back is dark green. The front has a padded section of dark green iridescent feathers overlaid with black net. The tail section of dark green satin is decorated with dark green iridescent feathers. The base of the bodysuit is decorated with black ostrich feathers. The whole body is lined with calico. The legs of dark green tafetta, terracotta satin, and royal blue felt are attached to the body by black elastic. The hem edges are slashed and are decorated with black ostrich feathers. Worn with wings and headdress ROH/PRO/COS/0003882 and tights ROH/PRO/COS/0005653.

searchDocuments.title: Boris Godunov [1869]
searchDocuments.subtitle: Opera | Modest Petrovich Musorgsky | Russian

metadata.After/based on: Adapted from the historical tragedy 'Boris Godunov' by Alexander Sergeyevich Pushkin
metadata.Notes: Musorgsky's original work, composed in 1868-69, consisted of seven scenes grouped into four acts. A revised version of nine scenes (six from the original and three new) was the first version performed, in 1874. After Musorgsky's death, Rimsky-Korsakov re-orchestrated the opera, making a number of cuts and insertions and transposing the last two scenes. This version was first performed in December 1896. Between 1906 and 1908, Rimsky-Korsakov worked on a second version, restoring the cuts yet retaining his own insertions. For many years, Rimsky-Korsakov's 1908 version was the 'standard version' used by opera companies worldwide. The original 1869 work was first performed in 1928.
metadata.World premiere: 16 February 1928, State Academic Theatre of Opera and Ballet, Leningrad
metadata.Related work: Boris Godunov [1874], Boris Godunov [1896], Boris Godunov [1908]

searchDocuments.title: Chevalier de la Légion d'Honneur (5th Class [Knight] of the Legion of Honour of the 4th Republic) Breast Badge presented to Ninette de Valois by the President of the Republic of France
searchDocuments.subtitle: Ninette de Valois Bequest | ROH/VAL/BEQ/08 | 1 May 1950

metadata.Description: Five-pronged star in silver and enamel, with the star's arms joined by green enamel sprays of laurel and oak. The central medallion bears on the obverse the legend 'République Française' and '1870' around a female head in profile ('Marianne'), symbolic of the Republic of France. The medallion's reverse carries crossed French tricolours and the inscription 'Honneur et Patrie'. The Badge is suspended from its plain red ribbon by an enamelled laurel and oak wreath. The ribbon covers a metal frame. Given in presentation case ROH/VAL/BEQ/10 and related to the Chevalier de la Légion d'Honneur dress miniature of the Badge ROH/VAL/BEQ/09, certificate ROH/VAL/BEQ/07, and letter ROH/VPP/1/25.
metadata.Dimensions: Medal: length 6 cm; Medal: width 4 cm; Medal: depth 0.25 cm; Medal and ribbon: length 10

metadata.Description: Cloak of gold lamé with a V neck and a train. The cloak fastens down the front and is lined in blue jersey. It has medieval-style deep slashed sleeves over fitted inner sleeves. The outer sleeves are lined in old gold taffeta with printed hand-painted decoration. There are lines of gold lace trim down the front with gold filigree mock fasteners, which also hold the slashed sleeves. The three-inch gold lace trim starts in a V in the centre of the back, runs over the shoulders, down the front, around the edges above hem level, and out to the back of the train. The trim is set with large faux rubies. There is a white cotton frill at the neck and around the inner sleeves at the wrists. Worn with dress ROH/PRO/COS/0004210, underskirt ROH/PRO/COS/0004211, underskirt ROH/PRO/COS/0004212, and crown ROH/PRO/COS/0000190.

searchDocuments.title: Commander of the Order of the British Empire (CBE) certificate presented to Ninette de Valois by His Majesty King George VI
searchDocuments.subtitle: Ninette de Valois Bequest | ROH/VAL/BEQ/01 | 1 January 1947

metadata.Description: The certificate reads: 'George the Sixth by the Grace of God of Great Britain, Ireland, and the British Dominions beyond the Seas, King, Defender of the Faith, Emperor of India and Sovereign of the Most Excellent Order of the British Empire to Our trusty and well beloved Edris Connell Greeting Whereas We have thought fit to nominate and appoint you to be a Commander of the Civil Division of Our said Most Excellent Order of the British Empire We do by these presents grant unto you the Dignity of a Commander of Our said Order and hereby authorise you to have and hold and enjoy the said Dignity and Rank of a Commander of Our aforesaid Order together with all and singular the privileges thereunto belonging or appertaining Given at Our Court at Saint James's under Our Sign Manual and the Seal of Our said Order this First day of January 1947 in the Eleventh year of Our Reign By the Sovereign's Command Grand Master Grant of the dignity of a Commander of the Civil Division of the Order of the British Empire to Edris, Mrs Connell. Related to letter ROH/VPP/1/01.

searchDocuments.title: Companion of the Order of the Companions of Honour Badge conferred upon Ninette de Valois by Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth II
searchDocuments.subtitle: Ninette de Valois Bequest | ROH/VAL/BEQ/47 | 31 December 1981

metadata.Description: Gilded bronze oval medal surmounted by a crown. The central gold plaque, depicting a mounted knight in armour, is enclosed in a blue enamel band bearing in gold the motto of the Order, 'In Action Faithful and in Honour Clear'. The reverse of the Badge is plain except for the crowned cipher of the monarch ('EIIR') in relief. The Badge is suspended via a plain ring from a red ribbon edged with gold thread fashioned into a bow, as it is a lady's award. The ribbon has a brooch attachment on the reverse. The Badge is worn at the left shoulder. Given in presentation case ROH/VAL/BEQ/48, and related to certificate ROH/VAL/BEQ/46 and file of papers ROH/VAL/BEQ/49.
metadata.Dimensions: Medal: length 7 cm; Medal: width 4 cm; Medal: depth 0.25 cm; Ribbon: width 10 cm; Ribbon and medal: length 12 cm

searchDocuments.title: Conchita Supervia Collection
searchDocuments.subtitle: Conchita Supervia Collection | 1888 - 1936

metadata.Date notes: The majority of the materials are dated 1888, 1893 and the period 1931-1936.
metadata.Extent: 1 box containing 2 photograph albums; 1 box containing 2 press cutting albums, 6 certificates and a diary; 4 loose mounted photographs; 1 loose mounted poster
metadata.Scope and content: The collection contains photographs, press cuttings, legal certificates, a tour poster, and a diary all relating to the personal life and career of Conchita Supervia. ROH Collections has additional material on Supervia: two artist files containing photographs, correspondence, press cuttings, and a programme for the 1934 concert at Queen's Hall; material in production files, and in the programme, poster, and press cutting collections.
metadata.Creator: Conchita Supervia
metadata.History/biography: Spanish mezzo-soprano Conchita Supervia (1895-1936) made her debut in 1910 in Buenos Aires with the Spanish Opera Company. Whilst in Argentina she performed in 'Blanca de Beaulieu' and 'Los amantes de Teruel' and featured as Lola in 'Cavalleria rusticana'. The following year she performed the most prominent role of her early career: Octavian in 'Der Rosenkavalier' at the Costanzi Theatre in Rome. In 1912 she sang the role of Carmen at the Gran Teatre del Liceu in her hometown of Barcelona. It was a role she was identified with for the rest of her career. Supervia starred again as Carmen in Havana in 1914, where she also appeared in 'Mignon' and 'La Favorita'. In the 1915/16 winter season, she sang Carmen again with the Chicago Opera Association, also appearing in the title role in 'Mignon' and as Charlotte in 'Werther'. For the next fifteen years Supervia confined her performances to Spain and Italy. This period saw her establish a strong association with Rossini mezzo-soprano roles, including Angelina in 'La Cenerentola', Isabella in 'L'Italiana in Algeri' and Rosina in 'Il barbiere di Siviglia'. In January 1932 she undertook a two-month tour to North America, consisting of concert recitals in Washington, D.C., New York, Montreal and Kansas City and elsewhere, and performances of 'Carmen' in Chicago and Boston. In 1931 she moved to London and married timber broker Benzion Rubinstein. In 1934 she made her Royal Opera House debut in 'La Cenerentola', and the following year appeared in 'Carmen', 'La Cenerentola' and 'L'Italiana in Algeri'. She had been engaged to appear in the Imperial League of Opera's 1935 autumn season at Covent Garden, but had to cancel her appearances as a result of her pregnancy. In addition to her opera career, Supervia made a number of recordings and appeared regularly in concert. She also starred in the Victor Saville film 'Evensong' in 1934. Supervia died during childbirth on 30 March 1936 at the age of 40. Sources: Sadie, S (ed.) Grove Dictionary of Opera, New York: MacMillan, 1992; record liner notes by Professor Stanley Henig at http://www. marstonrecords.com/supervia/supervia_liner.htm.; Rosenthal, Harold Two Centuries of Opera at Covent Garden, London, Putnam & Co, 1958.
metadata.Source of acquisition: Gift of Elizabeth Lloyd Roberts, 31 March 2009.
metadata.System of arrangement: The collection is arranged by material type.
metadata.Access conditions: The collection is available for viewing in ROH Collections by appointment only.
metadata.Language: English; Danish; Italian; Spanish; French; Hebrew
metadata.Copyright: Copies are available subject to copyright restrictions and the condition of the original material.

searchDocuments.title: Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire (DBE) certificate presented to Ninette de Valois by His Majesty King George VI
searchDocuments.subtitle: Ninette de Valois Bequest | ROH/VAL/BEQ/12 | 1 January 1951

metadata.Description: The certificate reads: 'George the Sixth by the Grace of God of Great Britain, Ireland and the British Dominions beyond the Seas, King, Defender of the Faith and Sovereign of the Most Excellent Order of the British Empire of Our trusty and well-beloved Edris Connell Commander of Our said Most Excellent Order Doctor of Music Greeting Whereas We have thought fit to nominate and appoint you to be a Dame Commander of the Civil Division of Our said Most Excellent Order of the British Empire We do by these presents grant unto you the Dignity of a Dame Commander of Our aforesaid Order together with all and singular the privileges thereunto belonging or appertaining Given at Our Court at Saint James's under Our Sign Manual and the Seal of Our said Order this First day of January 1951 in the Fifteenth year of Our Reign By the Sovereign's Command Grand Master Grant of the dignity of a Dame Commander of the Civil Division of the Order of the British Empire to Edris, Mrs Connell, (Miss Ninette de Valois), C.B.E, Mus.Doc'. Related to the Breast Star ROH/VAL/BEQ/13, Badge of a Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire ROH/VAL/BEQ/14, dress miniature of the Badge ROH/VAL/BEQ/15, and letter ROH/VPP/1/03.

searchDocuments.title: Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire (DBE), Civil Division, 2nd Type (post 1936) Badge conferred upon Ninette de Valois by His Majesty King George VI
searchDocuments.subtitle: Ninette de Valois Bequest | ROH/VAL/BEQ/14 | 1951

metadata.Description: Gilded Badge in the shape of a cross patonce decorated with pale blue enamel. The central medallion carries the conjoined profiles in gold of Their Majesties King George V and Queen Mary (as founders of the Order) within a red enamel band bearing the motto of the Order, 'For God and the Empire'. The reverse of the Badge is plain except for a central roundel bearing the King's cipher, 'GRI'. The Badge is suspended by a gold crown and ring and, as it is a lady's award, hangs from a bow of the ribbon, which has a brooch attachment on the reverse. The Badge is worn on the left shoulder. A Dame Commander is the 2nd Class of the Order. Given in presentation case ROH/VAL/BEQ/16 with Breast Star ROH/VAL/BEQ/13; related to the dress miniature of the Badge ROH/VAL/BEQ/15, certificate ROH/VAL/BEQ/12, and letter ROH/VPP/1/03.

searchDocuments.title: Diary of Conchita Supervia concerning her tour of North America
searchDocuments.subtitle: Conchita Supervia Collection | 1 January 1932 - 2 March 1932

metadata.Date notes: Dated entries cover 1 January-2 March 1932.
metadata.Scope and content: Diary containing brief entries describing Conchita Supervia's tour schedule, including travel times, rehearsals and performances, and her impressions of the cities she visited. The entries cover performances in Bloomington, Washington, Chicago, Grand Rapids, Boston, New York, Montreal, Kansas City, and Richmond. She frequently mentions her accompanist Boris Kogan and George Engels, Director of NBC Artists Service, who represented Supervia during her tour. Supervia used pages for October, November and December for making lists and sums.
metadata.Creator: Conchita Supervia
metadata.Dimensions: height 138 mm; width 120 mm; depth 37 mm
metadata.Copyright: Copies are available subject to copyright restrictions and the condition of the original material.

The dress has long sleeves slashed above the elbow to reveal grey lurex, and slashed below the elbows to reveal grey net and deep gathered cuffs. The skirt is cut away to reveal an underskirt of pink taffeta with an overlayer of net cut into squares and decorated with gold ribbon and diamanté. The skirt layers are trimmed with white fringing. Worn with train ROH/PRO/COS/0002144.

metadata.Description: Orange silk dupion empire line dress, with an inset collar made from pale pink net over bright pink satin. The collar and belt are embroidered with silver thread flowers and lilac beads, and edged with silver sequins on gold thread. The dress has long sleeves with three appliquéd flower shapes embroidered with silver and gold thread. Four long decorated panels ending in a point are attached to a flower shape and pinned to the front of the dress at the centre waist. The hem is trimmed with lime green rough linen with rows of sequins, two rows of metallic silver tassels and gold braid with silk covered gold bobbles. Worn with coat ROH/PRO/COS/0002419, collar ROH/PRO/COS/0002420, sleeves ROH/PRO/COS/0002421, headdress ROH/PRO/COS/0005741, and necklace ROH/PRO/COS/0005740.

The long-sleeved panelled bodice comprises a pale blue left-hand side decorated with black appliqué shapes on the sleeves and under the arms, and a pale grey right-hand side decorated with black appliqué shapes in the same position. The centre front panel of the bodice is black with three large pale blue buttons. The edges of the bodice, peplum, and cuffs are trimmed with a silver braid outline. The skirt comprises wide vertical stripes in blue and black, with crossway horizontal bands of silver lamé and black just above hem level. metadata.Description: Three-quarter-length silk dress. The long-sleeved panelled bodice comprises a pale blue left-hand side decorated with black appliqué shapes on the sleeves and under the arms, and a pale grey right-hand side decorated with black appliqué shapes in the same position. The centre front panel of the bodice is black with three large pale blue buttons. The edges of the bodice, peplum, and cuffs are trimmed with a silver braid outline. The skirt comprises wide vertical stripes in blue and black, with crossway horizontal bands of silver lamé and black just above hem level. The lower edge of the skirt is decorated with medallions of silver lamé suspended from braid. The Wardrobe Department labelled the costume 'Sevilliana Girl'.

The undersleeves of white net are decorated with gold braid and the cuffs with white rope braid. The overskirt is decorated with bows of dark green satin at the side and back. metadata.Description: Three-quarter-length silk dress. The long-sleeved panelled bodice comprises a pale blue left-hand side decorated with black appliqué shapes on the sleeves and under the arms, and a pale grey right-hand side decorated with black appliqué shapes in the same position. The centre front panel of the bodice is black with three large pale blue buttons. The edges of the bodice, peplum, and cuffs are trimmed with a silver braid outline. The skirt comprises wide vertical stripes in blue and black, with crossway horizontal bands of silver lamé and black just above hem level. The lower edge of the skirt is decorated with medallions of silver lamé suspended from braid. The Wardrobe Department labelled the costume 'Sevilliana Girl'. Worn with panniers ROH/PRO/COS/0003616.

searchDocuments.title: Dress worn by Frederick Ashton as one of Cinderella's Stepsisters in Act II of the Sadler's Wells Ballet production of 'Cinderella' (1948)
searchDocuments.subtitle: Costume Collection | ROH/PRO/COS/0001425 | 1948

metadata.Description: Yellow grosgrain and tafetta dress. The square neckline is trimmed with a frill of white net and decorated with zigzags of black grosgrain ribbon. The yellow grosgrain bodice is decorated with a pattern of vertical lines of black ribbon, hand-painting, and appliquéd black rings. The bottom edge centre front of the bodice is decorated with a large pale blue satin bow. There is a peplum of yellow taffeta overlaid with yellow net. The bottom edge is decorated with black hand-painting, black sequins, and gold baubles. The sleeves are yellow taffeta overlaid with yellow net, decorated with vertical lines of black ribbon and a horizontal band of black velvet with oval sequins. The cuffs are trimmed with pale blue satin bows and a flounce of white net hand-painted with black spots. The yellow taffeta skirt is decorated with vertical strips of wide black velvet ribbon, and pale blue satin bows on each side. Three-quarters of the way down the skirt is a hoop, and the line of the hoop is decorated with a horizontal band of net hand-painted black and with pearlised oval sequins. There is a row of scalloped tabs of black velvet with hand-painted yellow lines. The lower section of the skirt is yellow taffeta with vertical strips of black velvet ribbon. The hem edge is trimmed with black tasseled braid and black wool pompoms.
metadata.Creator: Jean-Denis Malclès

metadata.Description: Full-length medieval-style dress in rust-coloured silk velvet with a short semi-circular train. The neckline is trimmed with green satin ribbon decorated with appliquéd gold thread. The same ribbon runs in two lines down the front, framing the central panel. It has long oversleeves with a band of ribbon decoration around the top of the arm and at the cuff. There are long undersleeves in rust-coloured silk that end in a point over the hand. The dress is lined in rust-coloured silk. The belt of rust-coloured silk velvet is edged in gold metal thread ribbon and decorated with three glass aquamarines set in gold coloured decorative metal. The belt is made to appear to be tied with one end extending down the front of the costume. This costume was originally designed for a production from before World War II.
metadata.Condition: Good.The silk lining is degrading particularly around the sleeves.

metadata.Description: White crushed velvet dress with a round neckline and elbow-length sleeves decorated all over with star shaped sequins. It is trimmed along the neck edge, sleeves, and hem with gold coloured braid and faux pearls. The skirt is caught up at one side by an appliquéd crown and crest motif of silver lamé, pearlised sequins and gold braid to show a pink silk underskirt and three net petticoats. The skirt is trimmed around the hips with a cream velvet ribbon.

metadata.Description: Off-the-shoulder, three-quarter-length dress of ivory silk chiffon. The boned bodice is ruched and trimmed at the neckline with a band of gilt braid leaves set with faux pearls and faux amber stones. It has a central medallion of rhinestones and faux aquamarines. The waistband is made of dark brown net and two bands of gold braid and lace decorated with faux pearls and gems. The long chiffon sleeves are slashed and embroidered with gold braid in the form of fronds. The skirt is decorated with large opalescent sequins. There are elastic shoulder straps. Worn with headdress ROH/PRO/COS/0003462. [Note: Fonteyn first danced this role at a gala for the Royal Academy of Dancing in November 1959 and subsequently with The Royal Ballet in March 1960. She wore this dress in both productions.]

metadata.Description: Turquoise chiffon dress. The boned bodice has a base of beige fabric overlaid with ruched turquoise chifffon rising in points to the neckline where they are attached to a green braid, both in the front and at the back. There are green elastic shoulder straps. The front of the dress is decorated with white fabric flowers and green plastic leaves. The mid-length skirt has an uneven handkerchief hem line. Worn with headdress ROH/FON/COS/0003453. [Note: Fonteyn first danced this role at the world premiere by the Ballet do Rio de Janeiro in 1975 and subsequently with The Royal Ballet in 1976. She wore this dress in both productions.]

metadata.Description: Dress of gold damask devoré that has a floral pattern. There is a square neckline that is trimmed with a ruffle of cream silk and gold braid. The front and back panels of the bodice are laced together with gold cord. The under bodice has side panels visible beneath the lacings of a brighter gold damask. The sleeves are laced onto the bodice at the shoulders with gold cord. The sleeves are in two parts with the top part in bright gold damask edged in gold braid. The lower half of the sleeve is brown velvet edged with gold braid. The lower portions also have eyelets and lacings all down the outside edge. There are inset sleeves of a cream coloured chemise visible at the shoulders and between the upper and lower sleeves. There is an overskirt with front and back panels of darker gold damask and an underskirt of cream cloth that has side panels of brighter gold damask. The bodice fastens with hooks and eyes.

metadata.Description: Purple grosgrain tafetta dress. It has a collar of gold lace and gold crin. At the centre front of the neckline is a gold jewel with green oval faux gems. The full-length sleeves have a deep frill of olive green taffeta at the elbow. The skirt has a bustle of olive green taffeta that extends in swags over the hips and in flounces down the front of the skirt. The flounces are decorated at the sides and front with orange and black ostrich feathers, loops of black crin ribbon, and rosettes of red, turquoise and olive striped braid with a faux gem in the centre. The centre front of the skirt is decorated with horizontal stripes of turquoise grosgrain ribbon and gold braid, and baubles of orange sequins. The hem edge is decorated with baubles of orange sequins.

searchDocuments.title: Erasmus Prize certificate presented to Ninette de Valois by the Praemium Erasmianum Foundation, and related papers and presentation folder
searchDocuments.subtitle: Ninette de Valois Bequest | ROH/VAL/BEQ/31 | 17 December 1973 - 26 November 1974

metadata.Description: Erasmus Prize certificate housed in a dark red leatherette folder with the lettering 'EP' embossed in gold on the front cover. The certificate reads (in Latin): 'Amstelodami, die xxi mensis iunii anni mcmlxxiv DECRETUM Altissimus Princeps Regius Neerlandiae ex articulo ii legis Fundationis cui nomen PRAEMIUM ERASMIANUM, quo statuitur in singulos annos praemium praemiave decerni iis sive hominibus sive institutionibus qui humano cultui, societati, scientiis inserviant, itaque Europae unitatem vel unificationem strenue adauxerint aut in operibus suis demonstraverint, convenienter iis quae de mercedis usu in dispositionibus de praemiis adiudicandis praescribuntar, auditis etiam Viris consiliariis, confirmavit Moderatorum sententiam qua placuit ut PRAEMIUM ERASMIANUM ANNI MCMLXXIV decerneretur feminae clarissimae NINETTE DE VALOIS idque de causis quae separatim expositae sunt. QUIBUS DE CAUSIS PRAEMIUM ERASMIANUM ADIUDICETUR Feminae clarissimae NINETTE DE VALOIS praemium decernitur quia uno et perpetuo animi sui tenore id quod sibi aetate iam prisca proposuerat consecuta est, ut in Britannia societatem morem classicum secutorum conderet quae multis exemplo esset; quia rectam et veram viam secuta scholis saltatoriis quae per omnes nationes cognoscerentur conditis fundamenta, quibus haec res bene eveniret, iacuit; quia opera indefessa fiduciaque quam facultatum sociorum operis semper habebat effecit ut ei existerent et duces et magistri saltatorum qui toto orbe terrarum copiam sui facerent; quia non solum in omni genere plurimum ob omnibus postularet sed etiam ardore humanitatis suae exemploque excelso saltationis, choreographiae, institutionis et discipulos et saltatores et choreographos instigavit ut artem corde diligerent eiusque summum fastigium adipiscerentur'. The related papers are: a programme for the Erasmus prize-giving ceremony in Amsterdam on 21 June 1974; three typed copies, one annotated, of the address given by de Valois at the prize-giving ceremony; letters between Ninette de Valois and G Sluizer of the Praemium Erasmianum Foundation regarding travel arrangements to the ceremony and the distribution of the prize money, 17 December 1973 - 26 November 1974. Related to commemorative books ROH/VAL/BEQ/32.
metadata.Dimensions: Folder: length 33.5 cm; Folder: width 24.5 cm

searchDocuments.title: Frank Sharman Photographic Collection
searchDocuments.subtitle: Frank Sharman Photographic Collection | 1946 - 1951

metadata.Date notes: Material undated; dates derived through research.
metadata.Extent: 16 files of black and white prints (100 items); 14 files of colour transparencies (199 items); 22 files of black and white negatives (394 strips)
metadata.Scope and content: The collection contains colour transparencies and black and white prints and negatives of performances by English and foreign ballet companies performing in London: Sadler's Wells Ballet, Sadler's Wells Opera Ballet, Ballet Rambert, Les Ballets des Champs-Elysées, Les Ballets de Paris, International Ballet, Marquis de Cuevas' Grand Ballet de Monte Carlo, and Original Ballet Russe. There are also three images of the Covent Garden Opera Company. Sharman took many of the photographs from the theatres' balconies, although most of the colour photographs were taken during dress rehearsals from the stalls. The collection is notable for the colour photographs, shot with Kodrachrome film, which have retained their brilliant colour.
metadata.Creator: Frank Sharman
metadata.History/biography: English photographer Frank Sharman, F.R.P.S. (1904-84) took photographs of ballet companies performing in London between 1946 and 1950. Rare in a black-and-white era, Sharman used Kodachrome film to record ballet productions in colour, which has meant that the vibrancy and accuracy of the colour has lasted. Sharman also took black and white 'action' photographs of dancers during performance, usually shooting from the balcony. It is not known whether Sharman was a professional photographer in the 1940s, or trying to establish a career in ballet photography. His ballet photographs were published irregularly in 'The Dancing Times', 'Ballet Today', and 'Dance Magazine', and more frequently in 'Ballet Annual'. His images also appeared in International Ballet's souvenir programme for May 1950 and in the booklet 'The Story of Swan Lake' (E.G. Derrington, St. Clements Press, London, 1948), which featured International Ballet's production. Sharman joined the Royal Photographic Society in 1941 and it is believed he became a Fellow of the society with a panel of ballet photographs. He remained a member until his death in 1984. At the end of his working life, Sharman was the British agent for a German paper mill and a keen amateur photographer. He was President of the Beckenham Photographic Society, 1953-1955, and a member until 1971. Sharman was a regular speaker on the society's annual programme of meetings, and in 1961, he gave a talk entitled 'Twenty-one years of Colour'.
metadata.Source of acquisition: The collection was donated in memory of Ethel Sharman, wife of Frank Sharman, by her estate.
metadata.System of arrangement: The collection is divided by material type into three categories: black and white photographic prints, colour transparencies, and black and white photographic negatives. Within each series, the images are grouped by company and then alphabetically by production. All prints and transparencies have been scanned and attached to item-level catalogue records. A selection of images from the negatives have been scanned and attached to file-level catalogue records.
metadata.Access conditions: The collection, which includes large copy prints of 'The Sleeping Beauty' transparencies, is available for viewing in ROH Collections by appointment only.
metadata.Copyright: Copyright is owned by Royal Opera House Collections.

metadata.Description: Two-tiered headdress. The lower tier is black mesh decorated with silver effect braid, strips of diamanté, and roundels of faux jet decorated with silver effect cord, A row of round faux clear gems hang from the bottom edge. Attached to the sides of the lower tier are faux earrings of roundels of silver lurex with a central jet gem surrounded by silver cord and diamanté. Hanging from the roundels are round clear gems and black jet pendant beads. Attached to both sides of the lower tier are three strands of diamanté set in black which attach to a small round wire frame which sits on the back of the hair. It is decorated with a small oval jewel of black jet surrounded by silver cord and diamanté, a single jet pendant bead, and a plume of black ostrich feathers. The lower tier is connected to the upper tier by five stiffened supports of silver braid decorated with bronze coloured sequins. The upper tier is a wire frame decorated with silver cord and strands of diamanté set in black. It has seven ovals of silver lurex and jet gems decorated with clear gems, silver cord, and diamanté. It fastens with black cotton ties.
metadata.Dimensions: Crown: diameter 21 cm; Feathers: height 22 cm; Crown: height 19 cm
metadata.Creator: Barry Kay

searchDocuments.subtitle: Costume Collection | ROH/PRO/COS/0000178 | 1978

metadata.Description: Buckram cap covered with black lurex velvet. At the centre front is a green plastic jewel surrounded by blue, green, and gold sequins and green metallic braid. The front claws are black crin tubes filled with red, green, blue, and gold sequins, and the pincers are white crin tubes painted pink and filled with pink and orange sequins. They have pink metallic ribbon wrapped around the ends. The six legs are white crin tubes painted gold and filled with red and gold sequins and gold braid. In two places, they are wrapped with wire, which pulls in the crin to create the joints of the leg. Pink metallic ribbon is wound round the ends. The tail is a black crin tube filled with red sequins. In five places, thin bands of black lurex velvet wrap around and pull in the crin to create joints. Pink metallic cord runs along the top and bottom edge of the tail and forms the sting at the end.
metadata.Creator: Ian Spurling

searchDocuments.subtitle: Costume Collection | ROH/PRO/COS/0000133 | 1976

metadata.Description: Two-tiered headdress. The lower tier is black mesh decorated with silver effect braid, strips of diamanté, and roundels of faux jet decorated with silver effect cord, A row of round faux clear gems hang from the bottom edge. Attached to the sides of the lower tier are faux earrings of roundels of silver lurex with a central jet gem surrounded by silver cord and diamanté. Hanging from the roundels are round clear gems and black jet pendant beads. Attached to both sides of the lower tier are three strands of diamanté set in black which attach to a small round wire frame which sits on the back of the hair. It is decorated with a small oval jewel of black jet surrounded by silver cord and diamanté, a single jet pendant bead, and a plume of black ostrich feathers. The lower tier is connected to the upper tier by five stiffened supports of silver braid decorated with bronze coloured sequins. The upper tier is a wire frame decorated with silver cord and strands of diamanté set in black. It has seven ovals of silver lurex and jet gems decorated with clear gems, silver cord, and diamanté. It fastens with black cotton ties. Worn with armlet ROH/PRO/COS/0000135, wristlet ROH/PRO/COS/0000136, and choker ROH/PRO/COS/0000134.
metadata.Creator: Barry Kay

metadata.Description: Military-style jacket in dark grey wool check with a green and red fleck. The jacket has a short front edged in silver gilt braid, and a stand-up collar decorated in silver gilt ribbon. The jacket has gold epaulettes, silver coloured buttons, and a star decoration on the left breast. The full-length sleeves with split pointed cuffs are decorated and edged in silver gilt ribbon. There are three false silver gilt braid buttonholes with three silver buttons. The jacket tails are turned back to reveal a white wool lining. They are edged in silver gilt ribbon and held with one silver coloured button. The pocket flaps have three buttons, and there are two buttons to the centre back. The label reads: Regina.

metadata.Description: Black wool military-style jacket with a short front and stylised tails. The stand-up collar is of red wool edged in white wool crêpe and appliquéd with silver gilt stylised oak leaves. The gold epaulettes have gold fringing. The centre front panel of the jacket is of red wool outlined in gilt ribbon with large silver coloured buttons. The sleeves have deep red cuffs edged in white, with gilt appliquéd stylised leaf shapes and three buttons. The sash of silver gilt ribbon has a sword support and two tassels to the left. The jacket is lined in red chintz. The jacket tails have pocket flaps and three silver buttons, with two buttons to the base of the back. There is a deep vent to the centre back, turned back, with red wool edged in white.

metadata.Description: Short black velvet jacket. The neckline, centre front edge, and bottom edge are trimmed with mustard yellow velvet. There are eyelets and laces at the front. The sleeves are in two parts. The top part of the sleeves are black velvet with a wide mustard yellow velvet stripe, and are trimmed along the top and bottom edge with mustard yellow velvet. They are attached to the jacket and to the bottom part of the sleeves with mustard yellow velvet laces. searchDocuments.title: Lady de Grey Photographic Collection
searchDocuments.subtitle: Lady de Grey Photographic Collection | 1878 - 1917

metadata.Date notes: It would appear that Lady de Grey collected the photographs and postcards between the early 1880s and 1913. The earliest dated photograph is 1883, although research suggests that some items could be a few years earlier. The latest dated photograph is 1913. It is likely that Lady de Grey put the photographs and postcards into the two albums during World War I, when the Royal Opera House was closed and travel to Europe was difficult. Evidence for this is that the albums do not run chronologically, that her captions are in the same handwriting and pen, and in the past tense. Lady de Grey died in 1917.
metadata.Extent: 8 boxes containing 116 sepia photographic prints, 36 black and white photographic prints, 2 colour-tinted photographic prints, 15 sepia postcards, 6 black and white postcards, 1 paper postcard, 1 sketch, 1 magazine cutting, and 2 newspaper cuttings
metadata.Scope and content: Portraits of people in the arts, many signed and inscribed by the subject. The majority are studio portraits. There are two amateur 'snapshots' and two other outdoor photographs. Lady de Grey wrote captions under most of the images. The people depicted are: Singers: Emma Albani, Albert Alvarez, Max Alvary, Mario Ancona, Giuseppe Anselmi, Alessandro Bonci, Hans Breuer, Alois Burgstaller, Emma Calvé, Enrico Caruso, Lina Cavalieri, Féodor Chaliapine, Emmy Destinn, Ernest Van Dyck, Emma Eames, Fritz Friedrichs, Julián Gayarre, Jeanne Granier, Jacques Isnardon, Roxo Betty Kalisch, Jean Lassalle, Julius Lieban, Fernando de Lucia, Victor Maurel, Nellie Melba, Alice Nielsen, Lillian Nordica, Marguerite Zinah de Nuovina, Adelina Patti, Pol Plançon, Margaret Reed, Marie Renard, Edouard de Reszke, Jean de Reszke, Renée Richard, Anton van Rooy, Titta Ruffo, Albert Saleza, Sibyl Sanderson, Karl Scheidemantel, Antonio Scotti, Rosa Sucher, Francesco Tamagno, Heinrich Vogl, and Marie Van Zandt. Composers: Herman Bemberg, Arrigo Boito, Cécile Chaminade, Mario Pasquale Costa, Gabriel Fauré, Charles-François Gounod, Reynaldo Hahn, Ruggero Leoncavallo, Pietro Mascagni, Giacomo Puccini, Paul Alfred Rubens, Arthur Goring Thomas, Ambroise Thomas, and Francesco Paolo Tosti. Conductors: Tymoteusz Adamowski, Ernesto Bevignani, Cleofonte Campanini, Luigi Mancinelli, Alberto Randegger, Hans Richter, and Anton Seidl. Actors: Marie Effie Bancroft, Jeanne Bartet, Marthe Brandés, Lucien Guitry, Jane Hading, Cora Brown Potter, Gabrielle Réjane, and Ellen Terry. Writers: Alexandre Dumas (fils), Victor Hugo, Edward Bulmer-Lytton, Arthur Wing Pinero, Ernest Renan, and Jean Porto-Rico. Others: dancer Vaslav Nijinsky, artists Jean Béraud and Franz von Lenbach, impresarios Maurice Grau and Augustus Harris, musicians Mischa Elman and Joseph Hollman, opera director Pierre Gailhard, French statesman Léon Gambetta, mime artist Felicia Mallet, music publisher Tito Ricordi, members of the de Reszke family, and Lady de Grey herself.
metadata.Creator: Constance Gwladys (Lady de Grey) | Marchioness of Ripon Robinson
metadata.History/biography: Constance Gwladys Robinson, Marchioness of Ripon, was born the Honorable Constance Gwladys Herbert on 24 April 1859. She was the youngest daughter of Sidney Herbert, 1st Baron Herbert of Lea, and Mary Elizabeth A'Court-Repington. In 1878, Constance Gwladys Herbert married St George Henry Lowther, 4th Earl of Lonsdale (1855-1882), by whom she had one daughter, Lady Gladys Mary Juliet Lowther (1881-1965), known as Juliet. In 1885, Lady Lonsdale married Frederick Oliver Robinson, 4th Earl de Grey (1852-1923) and became Lady de Grey. When her husband became the 2nd Marquis of Ripon in 1909, she became Marchioness of Ripon (sometimes known as Lady Ripon). Lady de Grey was a leading London hostess and member of the Prince of Wales’s circle. Through her influence, Augustus Harris was made manager of the Royal Italian Opera in 1888, and the theatre’s fortunes began to improve after a period of decline. Lady de Grey’s patronage gave her influence over all major decisions, including the commissioning of new operas, the engagement of singers, and the granting of box subscriptions. She supported Harris in his decision to introduce performances of opera in its native tongue (when previously all opera was performed in Italian translation); this led to the company being re-named the Royal Opera House in 1892. Lady de Grey was friendly with many of the famous singers of the day. She was particularly close friends with Nellie Melba, whom she introduced to Covent Garden after seeing her perform at the Théâtre de la Monnaie. Following an unsuccessful début performance in 1888, Melba was initially reluctant to return, but with Lady de Grey’s persuasion she was encouraged to sing again a year later to great acclaim. In 1901 Lord de Grey acquired Coombe Court at Kingston, one of his many residences. This venue became well-known for the dinner parties hosted by Lady de Grey, to which singers from the Royal Opera House and notable figures were invited. Invitations were sent long in advance to ensure she obtained her ideal choice of guests. After seeing Diaghilev’s Ballet Russes in its debut in Paris in 1907, Lady de Grey was determined to bring the company to London, resulting in the historic season of Russian ballet at Covent Garden in 1911. It is said that Lady de Grey was present every time Nijinsky danced. When the activities of the Royal Opera House were halted during World War I, Lady de Grey devoted her time instead to the King George Hospital, where she worked daily caring for injured servicemen. Shortly before her death on 27 October 1917, she was working to establish a scheme for the care of paralysed and disabled soldiers near their own homes.
metadata.Archival history: The two albums were in the possession of Lady de Grey's daughter, Juliet Trevor (by her second marriage - Lady Juliet Duff by her first). Upon Juliet's death in 1965, the albums passed to her son, Sir Michael Duff. That same year, he gave them to Desmond Shawe-Taylor, the music critic and author, who had been a close friend of his mother. Shawe-Taylor initially bequeathed the albums to the Royal Opera House, but in 1992 he deposited the collection after conservation work. The conservation, undertaken by Kate Colleran and Marcel Ciantar in 1990 and 1991, involved removing the items and Lady de Grey's captions from the albums and re-creating the pages on archival boards with mounts. The conservators took photographs of the original pages, which were deposited with the collection.
metadata.System of arrangement: Lady de Grey compiled her photographs and postcards in two large leather-bound albums. During conservation, the images and her captions were removed and mounted on archival board, following their layout in the albums. Each page became a separate mount. The mounts are stored in eight boxes in the order in which the pages appeared in the albums.
metadata.Access conditions: The collection is available for viewing in ROH Collections by appointment only.
metadata.Copyright: Copies are available subject to the conditions of the originals and copyright restrictions.

metadata.Description: Brooch in the shape of a gold-plated rectangular bar with white enamel, bearing the initials 'TC' (Türkiye Cumhuriyeti - Turkish Republic). At its centre is an enamelled miniature of the Liyakat Misani medal: a blue, gold-plate, white and yellow star containing an artist's palette, a quill pen, and a microscope over which is a small red circle containing the Islamic motif of a star and crescent moon. Related to medal ROH/VAL/BEQ/68, presentation case ROH/VAL/BEQ/69, and certificate ROH/VAL/BEQ/53.

searchDocuments.title: Liyakat Misani (Honour of Merit) medal conferred upon Ninette de Valois by the President of the Republic of Turkey
searchDocuments.subtitle: Ninette de Valois Bequest | ROH/VAL/BEQ/68 | 1998

metadata.Description: Five-pointed silver star decorated with white and blue enamel and gold plating. Imposed on the star, at the top, is a red and white enamel boss with the Islamic motif of the star and crescent moon, edged in a wreath holding the letters 'TC' (Türkiye Cumhuriyeti - Turkish Republic). Imposed on the centre of the star, within a wreath of green enamel, are symbols of art, science and literature: an artist's palette, a quill and a microscope. The medal hangs without ribbon from a decorated brooch bar in white enamel edged in gold. The un-enamelled reverse carries in relief the letters 'TC Liyakat Misani'. Given in presentation case ROH/VAL/BEQ/69, and related to brooch miniature ROH/VAL/BEQ/72, and certificate ROH/VAL/BEQ/53.

searchDocuments.title: Magazine cuttings and ephemera collected by Nadia Nerina
searchDocuments.subtitle: Nadia Nerina Collection | 1940 - 1960

metadata.Date notes: Undated.
metadata.Scope and content: Black and white cuttings from magazines including pictures of the Sadler's Wells Ballet production of 'The Sleeping Beauty' featuring Beryl Grey, Michael Somes, Moira Shearer, and Jack Hart; cuttings from magazines of Sadler's Wells Ballet and The Royal Ballet productions of 'Swan Lake', 'Symphonic Variations', 'Scènes de ballet' 'Apparitions', 'Checkmate', 'Les Sirènes', 'Dante Sonata', 'Hamlet', 'Adam Zero', 'Miracle in the Gorbals', 'The Rake's Progress', 'Coppélia', 'Les Sylphides', 'Three-Cornered Hat' and 'Ballet Imperial'; cuttings of pictures of Anna Pavlova, Margot Fonteyn, Alicia Markova, Anton Dolin, and various dancers of the Sadler's Wells Ballet and Sadler's Wells Theatre Ballet including Pamela May, Brian Shaw, Donald Britten, Alexander Grant, Robert Helpmann, June Brae, Harold Turner, Julia Farron, Leslie Edwards, and Frederick Ashton; small poster of the Sadler's Wells Ballet performance at the Metropolitan Opera House, New York, 9 October-6 November 1949; Dance News feature on the first Sadler's Wells Ballet tour to the USA, October 1949; menu from the Dining Car Service enroute to Houston Texas on the Sadler's Wells Ballet tour of America, 1949; cuttings of pictures of the American Ballet Theatre productions of 'Jones Beach', 'Bourée fantasque', 'Les Présages', 'Rouge et noir', 'Pillar of Fire', 'Billy the Kid' and 'Graduation Ball' featuring Maria Tallchief, Rosella Hightower, George Skibine, Nora Kaye, Hugh Laing, and Michael Kidd; cuttings of pictures of Les Ballets des Champs-Elysées productions of 'Le Jeunne homme et la mort' and 'Les Forains'; cuttings of pictures of dancers including Marina Semyonova, Yvette Chauviré, Léonide Massine, Alicia Alonso, Vaslav Nijinsky, Marie Rambert, Constantin Tcherkas, Freddie Franklin, Alexandra Danilova, Patricia Miller, Pirmin Trecu, David Poole, Philip Chatfield, Elaine Fifield, Sheilah O'Reilly, John Cranko, Rowena Jackson, Tamara Toumanova, Mikhail Fokine; cuttings of pictures of various Russian dancers; a signed picture of Maris Liepa; greetings card from Ninette de Valois to Nadia Nerina, 6th May 1956; Christmas card from Cyril Beaumont to Nadia Nerina featuring a photograph of Marie Taglioni; colour postcards of San Fransisco, the Columbia River Oregon and South Africa; Wedding anniversary cards; Christmas cards; other greetings cards; 21st birthday card from Anne [Negus] and Beryl [Grey]; museum postcards of artwork; watercolour scenes and possible set designs by an unknown artist; cuttings of pictures of general interest from magazines.
metadata.Dimensions: length 39 cm; width 25.5 cm; depth 11 cm
metadata.Related work: Swan Lake Apparitions The Rake's Progress Coppélia Les Sylphides Le Tricorne

searchDocuments.title: Overtime chart for the technical stage staff of the Royal Opera House
searchDocuments.subtitle: Technical Equipment Collection | ROH/TEC/EQU/024

metadata.Date notes: Undated
metadata.Description: Single-sided board made of thick white cardboard with overtime hours written in marker pen. Staff names are listed in the left-hand column. The next three main columns reflect the working day, which was divided into three five-hour sessions: 8am to 1pm, 1pm to 6pm, 6pm to 11pm. When overtime became available, it was offered in strict order down the list of names, noting dates in the appropriate column. The board was kept outside the door to the OP (opposite prompt) fly rail, and removed from the Royal Opera House in 1997.

searchDocuments.subtitle: Poster Collection | ROH/MAR/POS/2247 | 21 November 1848

metadata.Date notes: Date of the performance, rather than of the poster's creation.
metadata.Description: Poster with black and red text, listing the casts as below. The top of the poster lists the ticket prices under the headline 'General Reduction of Prices!' The poster also announces forthcoming performances of the opera 'The Lady of the Lake' ('La donna del lago') with the ballets 'The Amazons' (Act I) and 'The Peri' (Act I) on 22 November, the opera 'Haÿdée' on 23 November, and 'The Lady of the Lake' on 24 November. The operas 'Quentin Durward' and 'Kenilworth' are in preparation. 'Kenilworth' by Francesco Schira (after the novel by Sir Walter Scott) was rehearsed but never performed.
metadata.Condition: Fair.Poster has been cleaned and conserved.

searchDocuments.title: Poster for a performance of the opera 'La Favorita' ('La Favorite') and the ballet 'Coralia, ou le chevalier inconstant' on 25 February 1847 at Her Majesty's Theatre, Haymarket, London
searchDocuments.subtitle: Poster Collection | ROH/MAR/POS/2239 | 25 February 1847

metadata.Date notes: Date of the performance, rather than of the poster's creation.
metadata.Description: Poster with black and red text, listing the casts as below. Of the singers listed, only the name Gardoni is legible; the others are derived from the poster for 27 February. The poster states that this performance is for the benefit of the Fund for the Relief of the Distressed Irish and Scotch, and 'in the course of the evening will be sung a lyrical ode written and composed expressly for the occasion'. Paul Taglioni choreographed 'Coralia' to music by Cesare Pugni, with scenery by Charles Marshall, the appointments by Edmund Bradwell, and costumes by Miss Bradley and Mr Whales under the superintendance of Mademoiselle Copére.
metadata.Condition: Fair.Poster has been cleaned, conserved and repaired. The right of the poster is damaged, obscuring some text.

searchDocuments.title: Poster for a performance of the opera 'The Castle of Andalusia' and the comedy 'Charles the Second' on 27 May 1829 at the Theatre Royal, Covent Garden
searchDocuments.subtitle: Poster Collection | ROH/MAR/POS/2258 | 27 May 1829

metadata.Date notes: Date of the performance, rather than of the poster's creation.
metadata.Description: Poster with black and red text, listing the cast as below. The poster states that this performance is a 'Benefit in Aid of the Funds of the Printers' Pension Society, for the Relief of Aged & Distressed Printers and their Widows' and that 'in the course of the Evening, an Address will be Spoken by Mr Keely in the Character of a Printer's Devil'. Between the opera and play is a 'musical melange' of songs and a piano concerto. The poster also announces the forthcoming performances of the comedy 'The Suspicious Husband' and masque 'Comus' on 28 May; the operas 'The Marriage of Figaro' ('Le nozze di Figaro'), 'Clari' and 'Giovanni in London' (Act I) on 29 May; the comedy 'The Beaux Strategem', divertissement 'Auld Robin Gray' and play 'The Invincibles' on 30 May; the play 'Romeo and Juliet' on 1 June; the opera 'Der Freischütz' on 2 June performed by Mr Schütz's German Company; and the opera 'The Maid of Judah' on 5 and 20 June.
metadata.Related work: Le nozze di Figaro The Beaux Stratagem Der Freischütz

searchDocuments.title: Poster for the Royal Italian Opera performance of a 'Grand Concert' on 30 May 1849 at the Royal Italian Opera, Covent Garden
searchDocuments.subtitle: Poster Collection | ROH/MAR/POS/2256 | 30 May 1849

metadata.Date notes: Date of the performance, rather than of the poster's creation.
metadata.Description: Poster with black and green text, listing the participants as below. The poster announces that the singers will perform extracts from the operas 'Semiramide', 'Lucrezia Borgia', 'Il barbiere di Siviglia', 'Don Giovanni', 'Lucia di Lammermoor', 'Don Pasquale', 'Masaniello' ('La Muette de Portici'), and 'Les Huguenots'. The 'Celebrated Pianist' Alexander Dreyschock will play a fantasia, 'the extraordinary Performer on the Contrabasso' Giovanni Bottesini will perform a solo, and The Hungarian Vocalists will sing 'two of their favorite morceaux between the acts'. The orchestra perform the overtures to 'Leonora', 'Semiramide', and 'A Midsummer Night's Dream'. The full chorus sings the 'Celebrated Prayer (without Accompaniment) from the Market Scene in 'Masaniello'.' The concert commences at half-past one.
metadata.Related work: Semiramide Lucrezia Borgia Il barbiere di Siviglia Don Giovanni Lucia di Lammermoor Don Pasquale Les Huguenots Fidelio

reviews and features of the South Africa tour, December 1959; previews for 'La Fille mal gardée' with a programme for the first performance at the Royal Opera House, 28 January 1960; reviews for 'La Fille mal gardée' and feature reviews in The Sphere, Ballet Today, The Dancing Times, February 1960; wedding invitation to the marriage of Princess Margaret and Antony Armstrong Jones, 6 May 1960; cuttings relating to the Royal Wedding, May 1960; cuttings relating to the news that Nadia Nerina is to dance as a guest artist with the Bolshoi Ballet in Moscow, August 1960; previews in the British press and reviews in the USA press for The Royal Ballet tour of the USA, September 1960; reports and features of Nadia Nerina at the Bolshoi Ballet , December/January 1961; British Journal of Photography feature of June 1961 Royal Ballet tour of Russia, September 1961; previews/profiles/reviews relating to the appearance of Danish dancer Erik Bruhn with Nadia Nerina in 'Swan Lake' at the Royal Opera House, March/April 1962; previews/reviews of The Royal Ballet Gala at the Royal Opera House featuring the new ballet 'The Rite of Spring', May 1962; searchDocuments.title: Roger Wood Photographic Collection
searchDocuments.subtitle: Roger Wood Photographic Collection | 1946 - 1983

metadata.Date notes: Materials have been dated from Wood’s negative registers or from research. A number of prints are dated on the back.
metadata.Extent: Black and white prints: 334 files of large prints and contact sheets; 158 files of proof prints. Black and white negatives: 230 files of 2.25" x 2.25"; 77 files of 4" x 5"; 45 files of 35mm (to date). Colour transparencies: 20 files of 2.25" x 2.25"; 37 files of 4" x 5"; 14 files of 35mm. 115 glass negatives. 16 files of documents (to date)
metadata.Scope and content: The collection contains prints, negatives, and colour transparencies of ballet, opera, and drama productions and portraits of dancers, singers, actors, authors, painters, and TV personalities. The majority of the collection concerns the resident companies of the Royal Opera House, and its touring ballet company. Wood’s photographs cover the Sadler's Wells Ballet/The Royal Ballet from 1946 to 1967, the Covent Garden Opera Company from 1946 to 1965, and the Sadler's Wells Theatre Ballet/The Royal Ballet Touring Company from 1946 to 1957. Wood also photographed other opera companies, such as the D'Oyly Carte Opera Company, the Glyndebourne Opera Festival, and La Scala Opera, and other ballet companies, such as de Basil’s Ballet Russe, Ballet Rambert, Grand Ballet de Monte Carlo, Kirov Ballet, New York City Ballet, Paris Opera Ballet, and the Royal Danish Ballet. In addition, he took studio portraits of many dancers, both in The Royal Ballet and in other companies. His photographs of drama companies are predominantly of the Old Vic and Royal Shakespeare Company. The collection also contains all Wood's photographs of Peter Hall's 1983 production of the Ring Cycle in Bayreuth, which led to the book 'The Ring: Anatomy of an Opera'. In the collection are Wood’s negative registers, some exhibition catalogues, papers relating to the negatives Wood deposited at the New York Dance Archives, and papers relating to 'The Ring' book.
metadata.Creator: Roger Wood
metadata.History/biography: British photographer Roger Wood (1920-2005) specialised in theatre photography and was particularly well known for his photographs of ballet. Born Alexander Roger Wood in Madras, India, on 6 August 1920, he attended Bradfield College, Berkshire, and became interested in photography at a young age. After World War II, his first photographic job was for Kodak as film production controller. In 1948, Wood left Kodak to set up his own photographic studio in Kensington. During this time, he photographed many leading ballet, opera and drama companies, and contributed to a number of books on these subjects. He frequently photographed productions at the Royal Opera House, as well as dancers in the Sadler's Wells Ballet, particularly Margot Fonteyn. From the 1960s and 1970s, he produced several books on North Africa and the Middle East. From 1974 to 1988, he also worked as photographic consultant to the Ministry of Information in Oman, and his advice and photographs helped to establish the national museums in Muscat, Doha, and Riyadh. He was an active photojournalist, working for Picture Post and Sie und Er, and contributing to the Sunday Times. After gaining a pilot’s licence, he worked for Sir Alexander Gibb and Partners, and other engineering firms taking aerial photographs. He was a Fellow of the Institute of British Photographers, the Royal Society of Arts and the Photographic Society. He married his wife Rosemary in 1986. Wood died on 21 June 2005.
metadata.Archival history: Wood gave each exposure of the black and white negatives a unique reference number, which he usually noted on the back of the corresponding print to allow cross-referencing between prints and negatives. The 2.25” x 2.25” negatives have a code of four or five digits prefixed with an A, and the 4" x 5" negatives a code of four or five digits prefixed with a C (for example, A32164, C6532). These numbers have been transferred to the catalogue as 'photographer's own reference number' on both the prints and the negatives catalogue records. Wood’s negative registers list the reference codes in numerical order regardless of the initial letter. The 35mm reference numbers have a six character code relating to the roll of film and the exposure. For example, 87V/320 reads as roll of film 87V/3, frame 20. For the purposes of cataloguing the negatives, the reference code is recorded only as the roll, e.g., 87V/3, while the records for the prints give the full code for each print, e.g., 87V/320. The 35mm negatives were housed in albums with paper inserts that act as the negative register. The initial numbers of Wood’s code explain the genre. For example, 82 was opera (albums 82, 182, 282) and 87 was ballet (87, 187, 387, 487). Wood did not give the colour transparencies and glass negatives reference codes, and the collection does not contain registers for these materials.
metadata.Source of acquisition: Roger Wood bequeathed his archive to ROH Collections, along with the copyright. His widow, Rosemary Wood, deposited the archive in 2006.
metadata.System of arrangement: The collection is arranged into five categories: black and white prints, black and white negatives, colour transparencies, glass negatives, and documents. Roger Wood divided his print collection into files of large prints of varying sizes, with contact sheets, and files of small proof prints (4.5" x 6.5"). The black and white negatives and colour transparencies are also divided according to size: 2.25" x 2.25", 4" x 5", and 35mm. Wood stored his archive in a variety of files and drawers, which in general were organised by physical format, then by company and production. This original structure was retained but refined into a specific genre order: opera, ballet, drama, other. Within opera, the Royal Opera House's resident company is always first, followed by other companies in alphabetical order. Within ballet, the Royal Opera House's resident company is first, followed by its touring company, other companies in alphabetical order, and ballet artists. Drama companies and other areas are ordered alphabetically by company, followed by people. Within each company, files are arranged alphabetically by work and then chronologically by production.
metadata.Access conditions: The collection is available for viewing in ROH Collections by appointment only. Original prints and paper materials are accessible. The negatives may be viewed at the discretion of staff.
metadata.Copyright: Copyright is owned by Royal Opera House Collections.
metadata.Condition: Good. A section of the 4" x 5" black and white negatives exhibit vinegar syndrome and have been scanned.

royal opera house, as well as dancers in the sadler's wells ballet, particularly margot fonteyn. from the 1960s and 1970s, he produced several books on north africa and the middle east. from 1974 to 1988, he also worked as photographic consultant to the ministry of information in oman, and his advice and photographs helped to establish the national museums in muscat, doha, and riyadh. he was an active photojournalist, working for picture post and sie und er, and contributing to the sunday times. after gaining a pilot’s licence, he worked for sir alexander gibb and partners, and other engineering firms taking aerial photographs. he was a fellow of the institute of british photographers, the royal society of arts and the photographic society. he married his wife rosemary in 1986. wood died on 21 june 2005. archival history wood gave each exposure of the black and white negatives a unique reference number, which he usually noted on the back of the corresponding print to allow cross-referencing between prints and negatives. the 2.25” x 2.25” negatives have a code of four or five digits prefixed with an a, and the 4" x 5" negatives a code of four or five digits prefixed with a c (for example, a32164, c6532). these numbers have been transferred to the catalogue as 'photographer's own reference number' on both the prints and the negatives catalogue records. wood’s negative registers list the reference codes in numerical order regardless of the initial letter. the 35mm reference numbers have a six character code relating to the roll of film and the exposure. for example, 87v/320 reads as roll of film 87v/3, frame 20. for the purposes of cataloguing the negatives, the reference code is recorded only as the roll, e.g., 87v/3, while the records for the prints give the full code for each print, e.g., 87v/320. the 35mm negatives were housed in albums with paper inserts that act as the negative register. the initial numbers of wood’s code explain the genre. for example, 82 was opera (albums 82, 182, 282) and 87 was ballet (87, 187, 387, 487). wood did not give the colour transparencies and glass negatives reference codes, and the collection does not contain registers for these materials. source of acquisition roger wood bequeathed his archive to roh collections, along with the copyright. his widow, rosemary wood, deposited the archive in 2006. system of arrangement the collection is arranged into five categories: black and white prints, black and white negatives, colour transparencies, glass negatives, and documents. roger wood divided his print collection into files of large prints of varying sizes, with contact sheets, and files of small proof prints (4.5" x 6.5"). the black and white negatives and colour transparencies are also divided according to size: 2.25" x 2.25", 4" x 5", and 35mm. wood stored his archive in a variety of files and drawers, which in general were organised by physical format, then by company and production. this original structure was retained but refined into a specific genre order: opera, ballet, drama, other. within opera, the royal opera house's resident company is always first, followed by other companies in alphabetical order. within ballet, the royal opera house's resident company is first, followed by its touring company, other companies in alphabetical order, and ballet artists. drama companies and other areas are ordered alphabetically by company, followed by people. within each company, files are arranged alphabetically by work and then chronologically by production. access conditions the collection is available for viewing in roh collections by appointment only. original prints and paper materials are accessible. the negatives may be viewed at the discretion of staff. language english copyright copyright is owned by royal opera house collections. condition good. a section of the 4" x 5" black and white negatives exhibit vinegar syndrome and have been scanned. metadata.Description: Watercolour and pencil design. The Pandur on the left is depicted wearing a red cap with a brown fur band, a red waistcoat with white frogging, a green jacket with white frogging, a green sash, cream breeches with a decorative pattern around the lower edge, and pale brown ankle boots. He carres a rifle. The Officer on the right is depicted wearing a pink cap with a brown fur band, a pink waistcoat with gold frogging, a pale blue jacket with gold frogging and brown fur trimming, a pale blue sash, cream breeches with a pink stripe down the outside leg, and pale brown boots. He carries a cutlass. Includes green, red and beige fabric swatches attached to the front of the design. The note '1' for the Officer and '6' for the Pandur on the front of the design denotes the number of costumes to be made from this design. A handwritten note on the front of the design reads: '1 officer, same colours as the soldiers'.

metadata.Description: Watercolour and pencil design for a Pearl Fisher who is depicted wearing a loosely tied white turban, hoop earrings, a green bead necklace, a red and white bead necklace, a sleeveless orange and red top, a white sarong with a red band, and a dark purple sash. He carries a dagger in his sash. The note '2' on the front of the design denotes the number of costumes to be made from this design. Includes a thumbnail sketch on the front of the design detailing a green and bronze beaded necklace. The wearer names noted on the back of the design are: Sampieri, Carra.
metadata.Creator: Attilio Comelli

The wearer names noted on the front of the design are: Pluys, Sergarit (unclear), Leclerc, Ragma, Dragers, Cullot. The wearer names noted on the back of the design are: Cravillon, Devandelaer, Pluys, Souchay, Menlendyck, Radamakers.
metadata.Creator: Attilio Comelli

metadata.Description: Watercolour and pencil design for a Young Woman who is depicted wearing a soft, full-crowned, pink headdress with a short white veil on the back and a short transparent veil over her eyes, a full-length mustard and brown dress with a black stomacher embroidered in gold, and pale pink sleeves with yellow and brown bands, a plain white apron, and a tasselled purse hanging from a brown belt. There are two quick thumbnail pencil sketches of different sleeves beside the main design. The note '4' on the front of the design denotes the number of costumes to be made from this design. A handwritten note on the front of the design reads: 'Chorus ladies soprani'. There is a list of wearer measurements on the back of the design.

searchDocuments.title: Signed and dated costume design by Attilio Comelli - Marguerite in Acts I, II and III of 'Faust'
searchDocuments.subtitle: Attilio Comelli Design Collection | ROH/COM/DES/COS/0162 | 1908

metadata.Description: Three watercolour and pencil designs for Marguerite. The half length design for Act I depicts her wearing a pink and white headdress, a short cape that has wide bands of dark blue and pale blue, a white shift and a white bodice with laced stays. The full-length design for Act II depicts her wearing a headdress of two pink, rounded horns, with a short white veil at the back, a white shift worn beneath a long pale blue gown with a laced bodice, full sleeves tied at the elbow and wrist with a blue and gold decorative border around the hem and bodice edge, and a narrow cream-coloured apron. There is a thumbnail design of the decorative border. The full-length design for Act III depicts her wearing a brown and grey headdress, a full-length grey gown with a laced bodice worn with a high-necked white shift, a full-length light brown cloak lined in grey, with a darker brown band near the hem and around the shoulders. The wearer name noted on the front of the design is: Madm Edwina. A handwritten note on the front of the design reads: '1 costume in grey. 1 small cape. 1 big cloak' and 'Piping same hue as gown'.
metadata.Creator: Attilio Comelli

searchDocuments.subtitle: Attilio Comelli Design Collection | ROH/COM/DES/COS/1119 | 1907

metadata.Description: Watercolour and pencil design for two members of the Female Bourgeoises. The full design of the character on the left is depicted wearing a headdress of a white wimple and a padded yellow and white roll around the head, a white chemise, a green under robe, a dark blue over robe with scalloped hanging sleeves, and a belt with a purse. The half design of the character on the right is depicted wearing a brown veil headdress, a white chemise, a brown under robe, and a camel coloured over robe with a decorative belt and cuffs. Includes thumbnails of the front and back of a different veil and bodices, and two decorative patterns. The note '4' on the front of the design denotes the number of costumes to be made from this design. The wearer names noted on the back of the design are: Wahdrey, Pizzi, Galhman, Mobine.
metadata.Creator: Attilio Comelli

The second character is depicted wearing a tall pale hat, a dark blue stock, a white winged collar, a pink and white checked waistcoat with a revere collar, an olive-green tailcoat with darker green lapels, and light breeches. The third character is depicted wearing a tall black hat, a white shirt, a black stock, a green and white checked waistcoat with a revere collar edged in dark green, and a pale coat with dark grey lapels. The fourth character is depicted wearing a white shirt, and a dark blue stock, a pink and beige horizontal striped waistcoat with a revere collar, and a coat with black lapels.

searchDocuments.subtitle: Attilio Comelli Design Collection | ROH/COM/DES/COS/0198 | 1902

metadata.Description: Watercolour and pencil design for a Peasant Woman who is depicted wearing a white turban headdress with a piece of red cloth running under the chin and over the turban, an ankle-length dark green skirt, a white apron decorated with a band of embroidery on the hem, a white, long-sleeved, round neck chemise, yellow gillet bodice with lacing at the front, a small brown purse, and pale brown shoes. She carries a basket of flowers. There are thumbnails of a different type of shoe and a bodice. Notes on the front of the design read: 'Bodice like this' and 'Bigger and not so elegant'. The note '3' on the front of the design denotes the number of costumes to be made from this design. A handwritten note on the front of the design reads: 'Bigger and not so elegant'.

searchDocuments.subtitle: Attilio Comelli Design Collection | ROH/COM/DES/COS/0301 | 1903

metadata.Description: Watercolour and pencil design for three Smugglers. The Smuggler on the left is depicted wearing: a red and white headscarf, a white shirt, a mauve bolero jacket, pink and grey diagonal striped overskirt, a pink underskirt with a ragged hem, a pink fringed shawl worn as a cummerbund, white hose and brown shoes. The Smuggler in the centre is depicted wearing: a black and grey hat with a pompom over a green and white headscarf, a white shirt, a brown sleeveless bolero, a brown and yellow diagonal striped overskirt, a mauve underskirt with a ragged hem, an orange cummerbund, an orange and green horizontal striped shawl over one shoulder, white hose and brown shoes. The Smuggler on the right is depicted wearing a pale grey bicorn hat on an orange headscarf, a white shirt with green sleeves, a grey sleeveless waistcoat, a maroon cummerbund, a blue and green diagonally striped overskirt, a blue underskirt with a ragged hem, white hose and brown shoes. The note '4' beneath the three designs denotes the number of costumes to be made from each design.

searchDocuments.title: Signed and dated prop design by Attilio Comelli - Radames' Triumphal Chair for 'Aida'
searchDocuments.subtitle: Attilio Comelli Design Collection | ROH/COM/DES/PRO/0006 | 1901

metadata.Description: Pencil and watercolour sketch with annotations depicting Radames seated on a gold and pink throne, decoratively carved with lotus flowers, chevrons, and sphinx heads. The throne is draped with animal skins and Radames' feet rest on a lion skin. The throne sits on a dais. Includes a side view of the throne. Handwritten note on the front of the design reads: 'These 2 props to be found from stock of CG. They will be carried by two singers. The lion and leopard skin from CG stock, also the drapery on the left side. Palms (unclear) also from stock'.

searchDocuments.title: Signed black and white photographic print of actress and soprano Jeanne Granier
searchDocuments.subtitle: Lady de Grey Photographic Collection | 19 June 1905

metadata.Date notes: Print dated from inscription.
metadata.Scope and content: Full-length portrait of Granier. She wears a dress of decorated fabric, and a fur and lace-trimmed cloak with a train. In black ink (faded) at the top of the image, Granier has written: 'A la Comtesse de Grey Souvenir affectueuse [sic], Jeanne Granier 19 Juin 1905.' Lady de Grey's label reads: 'The wonderful and versatile Granier.' The photograph was originally in album volume 2, page 51 (right).

searchDocuments.title: Signed sepia postcard of tenor Alois Burgstaller as Siegfried in 'Götterdämmerung'
searchDocuments.subtitle: Lady de Grey Photographic Collection | 1896

metadata.Date notes: Postcard dated from inscription.
metadata.Scope and content: Three-quarter-length portrait of Burgstaller in a tunic, armour, and winged helmet, holding a sword. In black ink on the left and right edges of the photograph Burgstaller has written: 'Blutbrüderschaft schwöre ein Eid'. Alois Burgstaller, Bayreuth 1896'. (The quotation is from 'Götterdämmerung'.) Lady de Grey's label reads: 'Burgstaller - a perfect 'Siegfried' '. The winged helmet seems most appropriate to Lohengrin, but Burgstaller did not sing this role until 1907, whereas he sang Siegfried in 1896. The postcard was originally in album volume 2, page 24 (top left).

metadata.Description: Short green brocade tunic cut longer at the right hip. It has a white jersey collar. The front panel is overlaid with net decorated with gilt ribbon and amber and pearl beads. The back is similarly decorated but not as heavily. There is an integral belt of leatherette squares and large faux amber stones, beneath which the tunic hem is decorated with a fringe of brocade oak-leaf shapes. The sleeves are slashed along the outside edge to reveal bronze linen and are laced all the way down. The sleeve heads are trimmed in brown fur.

metadata.Description: Dark cream brocade tunic with a V neckline. The collar and centre front are edged in yellow, black, blue, white and pink satin ribbon, with yellow and gold ribbon extending around the hem. There is an infill of pleated cotton trimmed at the neckline with two rows of pink ribbon. The jacket fastens with toggle ties of pink, blue and black cord. The sleeves consist of two bands of gathered cream nylon alternating with two bands of blue and cream brocade. Pink satin ribbon is laced over the cream nylon bands and fastened through brass eyelets on the brocade bands. The sleeves have white nylon cuffs. The jacket has a short peplum pleated at the centre back.

metadata.Description: Gold lamé boned bodice with a central panel of pink and green chiffon decorated with gold lamé ribbon, silver sequins, and gold and pink beads. It is also embroidered with three gold fleur-de-lys and a lion passant holding a pennant. The bodice is outlined in white faux fur decorated with black plastic diamond-shaped beads to simulate ermine. There is a frill around the neckline in white silk chiffon. The short puff sleeves of white chiffon are gathered with rows of false seed pearls.
